item.text: {"text":"Temporal attention has a clear foundation: [TiSASRec](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/wsdm20b.pdf) learns relative time-interval embeddings alongside absolute positions, distinguishing histories with identical item order but different elapsed times. It is an architectural precedent, not a BERT4Rec replacement for this task. More recent work, [Parameter-Efficiently Leveraging Session Information (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/10902109), introduces session tokens, session segment embeddings and temporal self-attention, reporting gains with little parameter overhead. [MIMAR-SRec (2026)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489) models evolving interests across contextual windows and robustness to temporal/preference noise. These results motivate testing temporal context; they do not establish that the supplied BERT4Rec suffers from stale-interest dependence.\n\nA compatible experimental hypothesis is one bidirectional BERT4Rec with jointly learned, per-head biases from bucketed historical time gaps, optionally conditioned on recent context. Compare against identical positional-only attention; treat adaptive recency weighting as an inference from the literature, not a verified improvement. Preserve masked-target training, appended-mask inference and final nonpadding readout. Use historical timestamps only: the unknown target timestamp must not determine mask-time features. Validate Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, then confirm checkpoint/exported-predictor score parity before interpreting interventions. Select using the fixed macro validation HR@10; use recent-history versus older-history ablations to test drift sensitivity. One jointly trained model and checkpoint per category satisfies the single-model constraint."}
